result.builder:
Build a new tool, jsonl-lint, as the first workspace under packages/ (the folder does not exist yet). Make exactly one pull request on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test that meets every acceptance line of https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/102.

Steps:
1. Create packages/jsonl-lint/package.json with "name": "jsonl-lint", "type": "module", "scripts": { "test": "node --test" }, a "bin" entry pointing at bin/jsonl-lint.js, and no "dependencies" (no runtime dependencies at all; devDependencies are not needed either). Plain ES modules, no build step, Node 22+.
2. Create packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js exporting lint(text). It splits text into lines (handle \n and \r\n), numbers them 1-based, skips lines that are empty or whitespace-only (they still count toward numbering), and runs JSON.parse on every other line, including a final line with no trailing newline (an unterminated/torn last line must be checked, not dropped). It returns an array of { line, error } objects, one per invalid row, where line is the 1-based line number and error is the parse error message string. A clean input returns [].
3. Create packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js (with a #!/usr/bin/env node shebang, executable bit set via git update-index --chmod=+x or chmod +x). Usage: jsonl-lint.js <file>. It reads the file as UTF-8, calls lint, prints one line per error to stdout in the exact form <file>:<line>: <error> (file as given on the command line), and exits 1 if there was any error, 0 if none. With no argument, or if the file cannot be read (missing), it prints a message to stderr and exits 2.
4. Add node:test tests under packages/jsonl-lint/test/ (e.g. test/lint.test.js) that cover: a clean file (no errors, CLI exit 0, no stdout); a bad middle row (error reported at the right line number, CLI prints <file>:<line>: ... and exits 1); a torn last row with no trailing newline (reported); blank lines (skipped, but line numbers of later rows stay correct); and the exit codes 0, 1 and 2 (run the bin with child_process spawnSync using process.execPath, write fixtures to a temp dir via fs.mkdtempSync(os.tmpdir()), test both no-argument and missing-file cases for 2 and that their message goes to stderr). Make sure node --test finds the files (default patterns such as test/*.test.js).
5. Create packages/jsonl-lint/README.md describing what the tool does, usage, output format, exit codes and the lint(text) API.
6. Update the root README.md: replace the "No tools yet" bullet with a list entry for packages/jsonl-lint and a one-line description.
7. Run npm install at the repo root so package-lock.json picks up the new workspace, and commit the updated package-lock.json; CI runs npm ci, which fails if the lockfile is out of sync. Then run npm ci && npm test at the root and confirm it passes and that the jsonl-lint tests actually run.
8. Open the PR with a body that contains the line: Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/102
9. Wait for the test workflow (.github/workflows/test.yml) on the PR head to finish; if it fails, fix it and push until it is green.
result.verifier:
Check out the pull request's head and run every check there. Run npm ci at the repo root first. Each check below matches one acceptance line of issue 102, in order.

Check 1. Expect: "packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file> prints <file>:<line>: <error> for every row that is not valid JSON (1-based lines, blank lines skipped, an unterminated last line checked) and exits 1 if any, 0 if none".
Run: in a temp dir, create clean.jsonl containing {"a":1}\n{"b":2}\n, and bad.jsonl whose content (with printf, no trailing newline) is: line 1 {"a":1}, line 2 empty, line 3 {bad, line 4 whitespace-only ("   "), line 5 {"c":3}, line 6 {"torn": (no newline after it). Run node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <path>/clean.jsonl; echo $? and the same for bad.jsonl.
PASS: clean.jsonl prints nothing to stdout and exits 0; bad.jsonl prints exactly two lines, one starting with <path>/bad.jsonl:3: and one starting with <path>/bad.jsonl:6:, each followed by a non-empty error message, no lines for 2 or 4 (blank lines not reported), and exits 1. FAIL: any other output lines, wrong line numbers, the torn line 6 not reported, a different format than <file>:<line>: <error>, or wrong exit codes.

Check 2. Expect: "A missing file or no argument prints to stderr and exits 2".
Run: node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js (no argument), and node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js /nonexistent/x.jsonl, capturing stdout, stderr and exit code separately for each.
PASS: both cases write a non-empty message to stderr and exit 2. FAIL: either case exits with a code other than 2 or writes nothing to stderr.

Check 3. Expect: "packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js exports lint(text) returning [{ line, error }]".
Run from the repo root: node --input-type=module -e "import { lint } from './packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js'; console.log(JSON.stringify(lint('{\"a\":1}\n\n{bad\n')), JSON.stringify(lint('{\"a\":1}\n')))".
PASS: lint is a named export; the first result is an array with one object whose line is 3 and whose error is present (a message); the second result is []. FAIL: import fails, lint is not exported, the result is not an array of objects with line and error, or line numbers are wrong.

Check 4. Expect: "The workspace has its own package.json (jsonl-lint, type module, test script node --test), no runtime dependencies, and node:test tests for a clean file, a bad middle row, a torn last row, blank lines and the exit codes".
Run: read packages/jsonl-lint/package.json; read the test files under packages/jsonl-lint; run npm test -w jsonl-lint (or cd packages/jsonl-lint && npm test).
PASS: package.json has name jsonl-lint, type module, scripts.test equal to node --test, and no dependencies entry (or an empty one); the tests import from node:test and contain cases covering each of: a clean file, a bad middle row, a torn last row, blank lines, and the exit codes; and the test run passes with those tests actually executed (non-zero test count, zero failures). FAIL: any of those fields wrong or missing, any runtime dependency, any of the five listed cases not covered, or the tests fail or do not run.

Check 5. Expect: "packages/jsonl-lint/README.md exists and the root README lists the tool".
Run: test -f packages/jsonl-lint/README.md; grep -n jsonl-lint README.md.
PASS: the package README exists and the root README.md has an entry naming jsonl-lint as a tool. FAIL: the package README is missing or the root README does not list the tool.

Check 6. Expect: "The change is one PR on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test whose body says Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/102, and npm test and the test workflow are green at its head".
Run: gh pr list --repo suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test --search 'issues/102' --state open to confirm there is one PR for this change; gh pr view <pr> --repo suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test --json body,headRefOid; at the head run npm ci && npm test at the repo root; gh pr checks <pr> --repo suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test to read the test workflow's check at the head commit.
PASS: a single PR carries the change, its body contains Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/102, npm ci && npm test exits 0 locally at the head, and the test workflow check for the head commit has concluded success. FAIL: the change is split across PRs, the body lacks that line, npm test fails, or the test check is failing, missing or not finished on the head commit.

Advisory
- Check that package-lock.json was updated for the new workspace (npm ci failing would show this too).
- Consider whether CRLF input and whitespace-only lines are handled, and whether the bin has a shebang and an executable bit; these are not pass/fail conditions.
